requirements.evidence: All contract items are present: app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9 (string-backed cases), app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:9 (extends RuntimeException), and the exact signature at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:17-21. Rules 1-8 are implemented: waiting-only/queue-scoped query (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:71-73), deterministic ordering (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:106-109), modes (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:77-92), fairness (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:115-133), persisted/locked queue state (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:25-31), dedicated exception per mode (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:37-38), lock-and-recheck loop (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:34-58), and the call fields set before return (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:53-56). Requirement 9 is met in docs/business-rules.md ("Call next:", "Normal wait limit", Call Panel table) and docs/architecture.md ("Call the next ticket" section).

conventions.evidence: Domain write is in an invokable action (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:15-21), docs are kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md, docs/architecture.md), and tests ship with the feature (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php). Deviation: conventions.md:92-103 requires CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] to be updated, and no CHANGELOG.md hunk appears in change.diff. Minor: conventions.md:102 asks for PHPDoc on touched public methods, but the public __invoke (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:17) has none while private helpers do.

security.evidence: No incoming user input or output is handled here; authorization is explicitly out of scope (task.md:11-12) and the docs state the boundary (docs/architecture.md:237-238). The action does not mass-assign: it assigns only the three permitted attributes directly (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:53-56), preserving the write-once rule, and all queries are parameterized Eloquent/query-builder calls. Queue state is re-read under lock instead of trusting the passed model (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:25-31).

tests.evidence: Good coverage of the main rules: priority ordering and returned fields (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:35-49), priority/issued_at/id ordering (:51-66), tie-break (:68-77), the three modes (:79-105), fairness forcing a normal (:107-122), fewer than three calls (:124-135), streak reset (:137-149), priority_only calls counting (:151-167), no normal waiting (:169-180), queue and status scoping (:182-192), stale queue rejection (:194-206), no-eligible-ticket per mode (:208-224), and write-once fields (:226-243). Gap: no test exercises requirement 7's lost-race path, i.e. the `continue` that skips a candidate already called concurrently (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:49-51), so exactly-once/skip-and-pick-next is unverified.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall with no speculative layers, but app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:53-56 re-implements the call transition (status/called_at/called_by_user_id + save) instead of reusing the existing Ticket::call() primitive named in task.md:5-6, duplicating domain logic the project already has. The double locking (candidate locked in the selection query at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:88 and locked again at :44-47) adds a step the task does not ask for.

readability.evidence: Small, focused methods (`__invoke`, `nextCandidateId`, `applyAnyOrdering`, `fairnessRequiresNormal`) with clear names (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:17-133); comments explain the locking and fairness intent (:23-24, :42-46, :69-70); early return/throw structure is easy to follow and there is no dead or debug code.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: the enum (app/Enums/CallMode.php), the exception (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php), the action (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php), the required docs (docs/business-rules.md, docs/architecture.md) and its tests (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php). No unrelated refactors, endpoints, or features.

issues.explanation: The skip-and-pick-the-next path required by task rule 7 (candidate called concurrently after selection) is never exercised, so the exactly-once guarantee is only argued in comments, not tested.
conventions.md:92-103 requires a Keep a Changelog entry under [Unreleased] for a new feature, and the diff does not add one.

The action duplicates the call mutation that Ticket::call() already encapsulates (status, called_at, called_by_user_id) as three direct assignments, so the two paths can drift and the write-once/enity-membership handling is bypassed.

The candidate is locked during selection rather than selected first and then locked as task rule 7 describes, which makes the later re-check almost unreachable and locks rows earlier than necessary (correctness is not harmed).
The new public __invoke has no PHPDoc while the private helpers do, but conventions.md:102 asks for PHPDoc on touched public methods.
Fairness history is queue-scoped, but no test asserts that calls in another queue do not count toward the three-priority streak (the cross-queue test only covers waiting-ticket selection).

review.summary: The change adds the CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException, and an invokable CallNextTicket action implementing deterministic priority/age/id ordering, the three modes, the three-consecutive-priority fairness rule, stale-queue rejection, and a lock-and-recheck transaction, with docs and a solid Pest suite. It largely meets the task and conventions; the remaining gaps are an untested concurrent-call skip path, a missing CHANGELOG entry, and minor duplication of Ticket::call()'s mutation, so it is approvable with small fixes.
